blueprint.primary_system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts

item.vignette: An 8-year-old boy is evaluated for declining school performance, behavioral changes, and progressive gait difficulty. Examination shows spasticity and hyperreflexia. He has diffuse hyperpigmentation. Serum cortisol is low and ACTH is elevated. Brain MRI shows symmetric posterior white-matter abnormalities. Plasma very-long-chain fatty acids are markedly increased, and genetic testing identifies a pathogenic ABCD1 variant.
item.lead_in: Which cellular process is most directly impaired in this disorder?

options.A: Transport of very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes for degradation
options.B: Transport of long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria by the carnitine shuttle
options.E: Schwann-cell production of peripheral myelin protein 22

explanation.key_explanation: ABCD1 encodes the peroxisomal membrane protein ALDP. Loss of ALDP impairs import of very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes, reducing their breakdown. VLCFAs accumulate and injure cerebral myelin and the adrenal cortex.

distractor_explanations.A: Correct. ABCD1 deficiency impairs peroxisomal VLCFA transport and subsequent degradation.
distractor_explanations.B: The carnitine shuttle transfers long-chain fatty acids into mitochondria and is not the ABCD1/peroxisomal defect.
distractor_explanations.C: Lysosomal sphingomyelin degradation is unrelated to ABCD1-mediated VLCFA transport.
distractor_explanations.D: Frataxin deficiency is the molecular defect in Friedreich ataxia.
distractor_explanations.E: PMP22 abnormalities cause inherited peripheral neuropathies, not adrenal insufficiency with cerebral VLCFA accumulation.

explanation.educational_objective: Associate X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy with impaired ABCD1-dependent transport of very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes, causing VLCFA accumulation, demyelination, and adrenal dysfunction.

evidence_map.claim: ABCD1/ALDP transports VLCFAs into peroxisomes; loss disrupts VLCFA breakdown.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Directly explains high VLCFAs, cerebral demyelination, and adrenal involvement.

evidence_map.claim: The demonstrated disease is specifically a peroxisomal ABCD1 transport defect rather than a mitochondrial fatty-acid import defect.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: ABCD1 localization/function excludes the mitochondrial carnitine-shuttle mechanism.

evidence_map.claim: The demonstrated disease is caused by defective peroxisomal VLCFA handling, not lysosomal sphingomyelin catabolism.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: The biochemical marker and ABCD1 genotype identify a different organelle/pathway.

evidence_map.claim: Reduced frataxin production is the molecular defect in Friedreich ataxia.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not explain ABCD1-associated VLCFA accumulation.

evidence_map.claim: PMP22 dosage abnormalities disrupt Schwann-cell myelin and cause inherited peripheral neuropathies.
evidence_map.item_specific_application: Does not explain adrenal insufficiency and cerebral VLCFA accumulation.

sources.title: X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: ABCD1 encodes ALDP, which transports very-long-chain fatty acids into peroxisomes; deficiency disrupts VLCFA breakdown and causes accumulation toxic to myelin and adrenal cortex.

sources.title: Friedreich ataxia: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: FXN GAA repeat expansion reduces frataxin production; frataxin is important for normal mitochondrial function.

sources.title: PMP22 gene: MedlinePlus Genetics
sources.supporting_passage: PMP22 duplication causes excess PMP22, disrupting Schwann-cell myelin formation and maintenance; deletion reduces PMP22 and causes pressure-palsy neuropathy.
